title: Pósa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
summary: We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $γ>0$, there exists $C=C(k,γ)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying \[ g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+γ\right) \binom{n-1}{k-1}p \qquad(1\le i<n/2) \] contains a Hamilton Berge cycle. The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic Pósa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.

title: Upper bound on the size of subgraphs avoiding cycles of girth length in graphs
summary: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-free if it contains no copy of $H$. The generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Turán number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Although $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$ has been extensively studied for various specific graphs $G$, such as hypercubes, complete transposition graphs, and doubled Johnson graphs, very few results are known for general graphs. For a graph $G$ of girth $g$, let $C_{g}$ denote the cycle of length $g$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, C_{g})$ for graphs $G$ in which every edge is contained in a fixed number of $g$-cycles, and establish a general upper bound on it. This bound generalizes the classical results on hypercubes and provides a unified approach for general graphs. Furthermore, we apply this bound to derive explicit upper bounds for several specific graphs, including $K_{n,n,\ldots,n}$, $K_{n}\times K_{n}$, $C_{m}\times C_{n}$, $S_{n}$, $AG_{n}$, $CT_{n}$ and $J(n;k,k+1)$.

title: Algorithms for Short Human-Verifiable Proofs of Non-Word-Representability
summary: A graph is word-representable if it can be represented using alternation of letters in words. The class of word-representable graphs generalizes several important graph families and admits a characterization via semi-transitive orientations. Recognizing word-representability is an NP-complete problem, and a major bottleneck in the theory of word-representable graphs is providing efficient justifications of non-word-representability of graphs, rather than merely referring to software verification. Recently, Kitaev and Sun initiated the development of methods for the automatic generation of human-verifiable proofs of non-word-representability. They introduced three algorithms and evaluated their performance on the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices, which constitute a fairly small sample set. In this paper, we confirm their ranking of the algorithms by testing them on all non-word-representable graphs on eight and nine vertices. We further introduce three new algorithms, one of which significantly outperforms the previously best method on graphs with at most nine vertices, producing substantially shorter proofs. We apply this algorithm to shorten a known proof of non-word-representability of the Shrikhande graph and to produce a proof of non-word-representability of a certain subgraph of the Kneser graph $K(8,3)$. This subgraph is the first known example of a triangle-free non-word-representable graph, presented in the literature with reference only to a computational proof. As a by-product of our study, we correct an error in the repeatedly published list of the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices.

title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
summary: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$. For these codes the stable profile is equivalent to minimality with the largest possible minimum distance; for even $m$ the analogous class consists of minimal MRD codes. More generally, for $1\leτ\le m-2$ and $\gcd(m,τ+1)=1$, we obtain nondegenerate $τ$-minimal codes of length $(τ+1)K$ for every sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $q$. We also construct maximum $h$-designs whose number of members grows exponentially with the ambient dimension at fixed $q,n,h$, and the associated maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes with a growing number of equal long blocks. In extension degree five, the ordinary and $2$-minimal constructions hold for every $q$ and every $K\ge32$ and $K\ge59$, respectively.

title: Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers
summary: We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration. A classical rooted-forest enumeration leads in both problems to $\mathcal T(x)$, the exponential generating function for rooted labeled trees. For $f=g\circ f\circ g$, the values on the cycles of $g$ determine all remaining values. The exponential generating function $\mathcal D$ for these ordered pairs and the ordinary generating function $\mathcal A$ for endofunctions up to relabeling satisfy $\mathcal D(x)=\mathcal A(\mathcal T(x))$. Finally, we count functions on $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ satisfying $f(ax)=af(x)$, first for prime multipliers $a$ and then for a broader class of composite multipliers. In each problem, fixing one map exposes independent choices for the other through its functional digraph or its fibers.

title: Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices
summary: Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$. In fact, rather surprisingly, in sufficiently large dimensions $d$ the number of vertices (equivalently, by duality, the number of facets) can be as large as theoretically possible, namely doubly exponential in $d$. These results were found using GPT-6.1 Sol.

title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
summary: We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $χ_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $χ_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts. The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.

title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
summary: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

title: Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $π/2+δ$
summary: For every $δ>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $π/2+δ$.

title: Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs
summary: Let $σ_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.

title: Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
summary: A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs. The former is characterized by ear decompositions. For the latter, we first characterize the $3$-connected case using the theory of line graphs and then extend the characterization to the general case by a suitable $2$-sum operation.

title: Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas
summary: We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes. We determine exact eventual formulas when the fixed set has six, seven or eight items. The eight-item formula has a period-three correction. We explain this correction by optimizing the sizes of shared test pieces within fixed decision-tree prefixes. For each fixed finite family of such prefixes ending in star forests, the optimal deficit is eventually a rational polynomial plus a bounded periodic function. The asymptotic proofs are analytic; the exact formulas also use integer constructions and rational exclusion certificates.

title: The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues
summary: For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$. The construction combines faithful stress-free Gram representations, a one-coordinate lift for each excess core edge, exact orthogonal-frame completion, and a Stiefel-manifold pendant-extension argument.

title: Every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most 6
summary: We prove that every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most $6$. Weak-strict degeneracy is the weak degeneracy of Bernshteyn and Lee plus one, so it bounds the coloring parameters controlled by weak degeneracy. In particular, every IC-planar graph is $6$-choosable, $6$-DP-colorable and $6$-paintable, which strengthens the theorem of Yang, Wang, Wang and Lih that IC-planar graphs are $6$-choosable. An IC-planar graph is a subgraph of a plane graph in which a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint inner $4$-faces, called marked faces, receive both diagonals. Our main tool is a Thomassen-type statement for such graphs: vertices of marked faces get one extra unit, except those in a prescribed independent set of boundary vertices. With no marked faces, this statement is exactly the theorem of Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge that gives weak-strict degeneracy at most $5$ for planar graphs, so it contains both results. We prove it by a minimal-counterexample argument following Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge. The new ingredients are a deletion rule that turns destroyed marked faces into ordinary edges, a pseudo-$2$-chord lemma for paths that use one diagonal, and a choice of orientation of the outer cycle that avoids a vertex of the independent set joined to two vertices of the prescribed boundary path.

title: A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph
summary: In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_2}\). We rigorously prove its Petersen-free property, thereby improving the previously documented lower bound to \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}) \ge 21\). Furthermore, we demonstrate the limit of this structural family by showing that the natural extension \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_3}\) contains a Petersen subgraph.

title: On the Motzkin-Straus theorem and clique number for k-uniform hypergraphs
summary: In this paper, we establish a Motzkin-Straus type equality for k-uniform hypergraphs under certain conditions, which extends the classical Motzkin--Straus theorem for graphs. Using this equality, we present several spectral bounds for the clique number of k-uniform hypergraphs in terms of the spectral radii of the adjacency, signless Laplacian, and Laplacian tensors. When k=2, the bounds coincide with the corresponding known results for graphs.

title: A 4-regular graph with 4/5 of its vertices satisfying the Šoltés property
summary: The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of its vertices. A vertex $v$ is called a Šoltés vertex if $G-v$ is connected and $W(G-v)=W(G)$. Since the cycle $C_{11}$ is the only known graph in which every vertex is a Šoltés vertex, a natural problem is to construct other graphs with as large a proportion of such vertices as possible. We construct a $4$-regular graph with Šoltés fraction $4/5$, improving the previous value of $2/3$.

title: Mutual-visibility in (d, 5)-graphs with excess
summary: The author investigates mutual visibility in regular graphs of girth at least 5, with particular emphasis on graphs with excess. A general upper bound on the mutual-visibility number is established in terms of the degree and order. More significantly, an algebraic inequality is derived that restricts the mutual-visibility number of $(d,5,+δ)$-graphs. As applications, the mutual-visibility number of the Robertson graph is shown to be 9, and upper bounds are obtained for the $(5,5)$-cages and the $(6,5)$-cage.

title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
summary: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.

title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
summary: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane developed by Haiman.

title: The maximum size of $3$-distance binary codes
summary: In this paper, we show that for every positive integer $n \ge 24$, the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of vectors from $\{-1,1\}^n$ with at most three distinct Hamming distances is equal to $\binom{n}{3}+n$. The threshold $n=24$ is best possible.

title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
summary: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$. The resulting score has mean $(3/2)^d$ for every partition, while its distribution reflects the geometry of the tiling. Comparing two such scores, with the shifts chosen independently, defines a game in which the larger score wins. In dimension $d=4$, we construct a geometric realization of the Steinhaus--Trybuła paradox: three periodic partitions form a cycle in which each beats the next with probability strictly greater than $1/2$. We describe local configurations by finite cube tiling codes and prove that every resulting list of counts is majorized by that of the simple code $C_d=\{0,2\}^d$. Nevertheless, every non-simple code differing from $C_d$ in only two coordinate directions beats it, with a sharp lower bound on the winning margin. We also show that the ratio of wins to losses of $C_d$ has limit superior at most $1$ as the dimension tends to infinity, uniformly over opposing codes. For $4\mathbb{Z}^d$-periodic tilings, changing the window size can repeatedly reverse the winner, but the winning margin eventually stabilizes separately for side lengths $4m+1$ and $4m+3$.

title: Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erdős--Straus conjecture
summary: For the Erdős--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))$, an algebraic and spectral container hierarchy combined with a generating-polynomial large sieve reaches the exponent $1-o(1)$: $|E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))|\ll_κN\exp(-(\frac{1}{40960}+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)^κ})$, matching the CRT capacity scale. These results resolve the obstructions to composite-witness sieving at growing depth. First, we replace subgroup generation by Kneser's stabilizer $K(M)$, which embeds into a $2$-primary character kernel, reducing container counts from $2^{Θ(J^{4})}$ to $\exp(\mathcal{O}(J^{2}\log\log J))$. Coupling this with a generating-polynomial large sieve, Markov $1/2$-popular symmetry containers, and Pontryagin--Plancherel character containers yields the exponent $1-o(1)$ on $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}$. Second, to bypass unlocalized diffuse divisor sheets without subset enumeration, we construct a semi-composite congruence sieve $s=pq\equiv-1\pmod{12ua}$ ($p\in(Z^{9/10},Z]$, $q\le Q$ rough). Conditioning on $n\bmod M_{\mathrm{small}}$ yields CRT mutual independence while decoupling the modulus $12ua\le 12Z^{1/4}$ from $q$; a Bonferroni majorant and the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem then yield the unconditional $5/7$ exponent on all of $E(N)$. Finally, we study bilinear dispersion on $4uavw-4u^{2}v-w=n$ and difference sets $D(K_c)$.

title: Burgess' bounds with prime moduli
summary: Let $S_χ(N)= \sum_{n\leq N} χ(n)$, where $χ$ is a Dirichlet character modulo a prime $p$. For integral $r\geq 2$, Burgess gave bounds of the shape $S_χ(N) \ll N^{1-1/r} p^{(r+1)/(4r^{2})} \log p$. The factor of $\log p$ was reduced by several authors. We show that it can be removed completely.

title: Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group
summary: For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.

title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
summary: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II
summary: We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different. Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.

title: Campana points on quadrics with hyperplane boundary
summary: Let $Q\subset\mathbf P^{d+1}_k$ be a smooth quadric of dimension $d\ge2$ over a number field, and let $H_i=Q\capΠ_i$ be hyperplane sections for $1\le i\le d$. For every integer $m\ge2$, we prove Campana strong approximation for the pair $\bigl(Q,(1-1/m)(H_1+\cdots+H_d)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)$.

title: Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two
summary: Let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Dx$ have rank two and let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be a prime of good reduction. We study the conjecture that the $p$-adic quotient $q_p$, the leading coefficient of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function divided by the Euler factor and the $p$-adic regulator, equals the complex quotient $q_\infty=L''(E,1)/(2Ω_E\mathrm{Reg}_\infty)$, and that the latter is rational. In rank one the analogous statement is a theorem of Perrin-Riou and Rubin, because a Heegner point computes both sides; in rank two there is no such point. We show that $q_p$ is the constant of the quadratic term of the two-variable Katz measure; this is how the conjecture arises, and it computes $q_p$ modulo any power of $p$ from critical Hecke $L$-values. We then show that $q_p$ is the coordinate of two global classes: Rubin's rank-two elliptic-unit class, whose position in $E(\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}_p$ is $q_p$ times an explicit vector, and the derived Heegner class over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field $F$, for which we prove an exact identity. As consequences, whenever such a field $F$ satisfying our hypotheses exists, $q_p$ is a square in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ times the product of the Tamagawa numbers of $E$, so that the unit $q_p/A_E$ of the $p$-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula is a square when Sha is finite; if moreover the derived Heegner class has non-zero formal logarithm, the conjecture of Agboola and Castella for $E/F$ holds up to a $p$-adic unit, and with a theorem of Burungale, Castella and Skinner the anticyclotomic main conjecture holds integrally; and our conjecture is equivalent to the analytic form of theirs, with the products of anticyclotomic heights read sesquilinearly, which differs by a sign from its literal formulation. The conjecture is verified modulo $p^3$ for 5520 pairs $(E,p)$ with conductors up to $3.9\cdot10^{12}$, including curves with analytic Sha of order 4 and 9.

title: Bounded Ratios of Best Approximations: Sharp Bounds and Spectra of Diophantine Exponents
summary: We solve Problems 1, 2, and 3 posed by Marnat, Moshchevitin, and Schleischitz (arXiv:2505.15964). We consider totally irrational real n-by-m matrices and two conditions on their sequences of best approximations: (B) bounded successive height ratios and (C) bounded successive error ratios. Under (C), we prove that the ordinary Diophantine exponent is at most m and, when both dimensions are at least two, that the uniform exponent is at most m^2/(m+1). Combining these bounds with known results, we determine the individual spectra of both exponents under (C), with and without the additional assumption (B). When both dimensions are at least two, imposing (B) changes neither spectrum. A key ingredient is a block lemma for consecutive best approximations lying in a fixed rational subspace.

title: Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials
summary: Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach à la Skolem, that for a root $α\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(α)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.

title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
summary: Let $φ$ be a fixed polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and degree $k\geq2$. We prove that the values $2φ(n)$, $1\leq n\leq N$, can be written as the sum of two primes, apart from at most $N^{α_k+o(1)}$ exceptional indices, where $α_k<1$. For quadratic polynomials the exponent is $1/2$, for cubic polynomials $5/8$, for quartic polynomials $3/4$, and for $k>4$ it is $1-1/(k+1)$. The proof combines a fourth-moment estimate over primes with mean-value estimates over arbitrary subsets of polynomial sequences.

title: Curves with absolutely irreducible Tate modules over $p$-adic fields
summary: Over every number field, curves whose Jacobians have absolutely irreducible $\ell$-adic Tate modules exist in every positive genus and can be chosen hyperelliptic. Over $p$-adic fields, however, inertia and Frobenius can exclude entire genera. We classify the genera that occur for $\ell\ne p$ in terms of the residue characteristic and the cardinality of the residue field. For odd $p$, we also classify the genera occurring for hyperelliptic curves. These genera have relative density zero among those occurring for arbitrary curves, yielding Jacobians whose isogeny classes contain no hyperelliptic Jacobian. For odd $p$ and even residue degree, we obtain further restrictions on the genus when the curve itself is required to have potentially good reduction. Over number fields, we obtain uniform bounds from absolute irreducibility of the Tate module at two finite places of distinct residue characteristics different from $\ell$. The dimension of the abelian variety alone bounds the number of isomorphism classes in its isogeny class and the least degrees of isogenies between them.

title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
summary: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power $q$, consider polynomials over $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ of the form $\sum_{0\le i\le j<n}a_{ij}x^{q^i+q^j}+L(x)$, where $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_{q^n}$ and $L$ serves as an $\mathbb F_q$-linear endomorphism of $\mathbb F_{q^n}$. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

title: On a Problem of Gordon and Hughes: The 11-adic Properties of Meromorphic Modular Functions on $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$
summary: Congruence families occur throughout the theory of modular forms. These families superficially resemble one another, though they can vary substantially in their overall difficulty. One major complication resides in the topology of the modular curve associated with a given congruence family. All previously studied families are associated with curves of genus 0 or 1. The existence of a family associated with a curve of genus 2 (and the associated difficulties of a proof thereof) was first speculated upon by Gordon and Hughes. We give the first explicit congruence family associated with $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$, a modular curve of genus 2, and prove it. We also propose two families of conjectures associated with the same modular curve.

title: Euler trace congruences over local fields
summary: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\QQ_p$ with uniformizer $π$ and residue field $\FF_q$. For each $r\ge1$, we determine the largest integer $E_r$ such that $\Tr(A^{q^r})\equiv\Tr(A^{q^{r-1}})\pmod{π^{E_r}}$ for every integral matrix $A$ with a prescribed residual similarity class. We give formulas for both nilpotent and nonnilpotent residual classes and construct integral lifts attaining the resulting exponents. We also exhibit local fields with the same ramification index and residue field for which the optimal exponents differ, even when $r$ and the residual similarity class are fixed.

title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
summary: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

title: Mellin Transform formulas for special values of Goss $L$-functions
summary: In the present paper, we provide formulas for the special values of dual Goss $L$-functions of Drinfeld modules at any non-negative integer in terms of the determinant of the values of a motivic map, extensively studied by both authors in 2026, for a large class of Anderson modules. Our result may be seen as a function field analogue of conjectural formulas for special values of motivic $L$-functions in terms of algebraic Mellin integrals.

title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
summary: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\llη\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.

title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
summary: We determine sharp universality thresholds for quotients of the free profinite group $\widehat F_n$ on $n$ generators by $n+u$ independent random relations, where $u$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. For products of mutually independent uniformly coset-balanced factors, convergence to the Liu--Wood measure $μ_u$ holds when the minimum number of factors grows faster than $\log n$, which is a uniformly sharp condition. For random words of fixed length $\ell_n$, convergence holds exactly when $\ell_n$ is eventually odd and $\ell_n-\log n\to\infty$. We also prove universality for randomly ordered products of independent integer powers under the balance condition $nα_{n,p}/\log n\to\infty$ at each fixed prime, recovering finite-prime cokernel laws by abelianization.

title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
summary: We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.
